content.overview: Git submodules and subtrees allow you to include other Git repositories within your main repository. This is useful for managing dependencies and incorporating external code into your project.

steps.title: Understanding Git Submodules
steps.content: Git submodules allow you to keep a Git repository as a subdirectory of another Git repository. This lets you include external code in your project while keeping it separate and maintaining its own history.

steps.title: Adding a Submodule
steps.content: To add a submodule to your repository, use the `git submodule add` command followed by the repository URL and the path where you want the submodule to be placed.

steps.title: Cloning a Repository with Submodules
steps.content: When you clone a repository that contains submodules, you need to initialize and update the submodules to get their contents.

steps.title: Working with Git Subtrees
steps.content: Git subtrees are an alternative to submodules. They allow you to include the contents of another repository into your main repository, but without the complexity of submodules.

commands.expectedOutput:

behindTheCommand.title: Submodules vs. Subtrees
behindTheCommand.content:
Submodules and subtrees are two different approaches to including external repositories in your project:

- **Submodules** store a reference to a specific commit in the external repository. They require extra steps when cloning and updating, but keep a clear separation between your code and the external code.

- **Subtrees** actually copy the external code into your repository. This makes cloning and working with the repository simpler, but can make the history more complex when you update the external code.
